analysis: Examined ProviderLoop+InferenceHandler.swift. The only changes (complete range map) rename the autopilot admission predicate from autopilotAllowsModel to autopilotServesModel at head lines 135 (local-work gate throwIfRefusingNewLocalWork) and 513 (authoritative network admission check before inference_accepted). Surrounding behavior is unchanged. Decryption, sender-key validation, tool-schema metadata rejection, deadline checks, drain re-checks, receipt finalizer settlement, billing floors, response attestation and cache-usage reporting (T-041 cacheScope coordinator-authored, never caller-controlled) are untouched. This is an availability/placement gate, not an authorization, encryption or attestation control in the threat model. The prefix-cache salt plumbing is unchanged; the prompt_cache_key exclusion at line 403 is unchanged. Base unit 4 (lines 1144-1556) covers the streaming, hash, usage and billing paths, with no diff there. Integration question: the semantics of autopilotServesModel versus autopilotAllowsModel are defined elsewhere and not supplied. If the new predicate is more permissive (e.g., admits models outside the operator's selection), it could affect local/network admission. However, that change would be capacity/placement policy, not a TB-002/TB-011 trust control. The coordinator's routing and App Attest authorization remain authoritative. There is no evidence of a security regression, so no finding is reported.
